messages.subject: Renjin On Android
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was curious if it would be possible to get Renjin running on Android. I saw that the topic has been briefly discussed <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/renjin-dev/jrpvg6ycNes> previously. Alex mentioned that certain limitations of the Dalvik VM might be a challenge. And indeed as expected I ran into an issue, specifically Android only supports Java 1.6, but right now Renjin requires Java 7. If I understand the commit history correctly this was introduced to support MethodHandler <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/73fd548>. And indeed I am able to get Renjin kind of running (there are errors, but they look like I could fix them) up to version 0.7.1579. Later versions simply don't compile due to the mentioned version incompatibility.
My question now is, what was the main motivation behind this change? Would it be possible in your opinion to patch my own Renjin so it would use for example reflection instead of Methodhandlers? Or what would be the main featues, that I would be loosing if I would rebase my development  for Android on top of Renjin 0.7.1579?
I hope you can share some of your insights on the topics.

Best Regards,
Artjom Metro

messages.subject: Re: xgboost
messages.body_plain:
Hi David,

glad to hear that you're excited about Renjin!

It looks like xgboost has never been successfully compiled for Renjin. This is partly due to the package's internal C++ code which our transpiler isn't yet able to convert to Java bytecode, but also due to the unavailability of its dependencies. Unfortunately, these aren't minor dependencies either as data.table, for example, uses GNU R's C API in very "creative" ways and thus will be a challenge to compile for Renjin. But this is not to say that it's impossible to get xgboost to work in Renjin.

If you are of the inpatient type, a quicker option could be to wrap a pure-Java implementation <https://github.com/komiya-atsushi/xgboost-predictor-java> in an R package for Renjin. Our documentation includes pointers on how to create extension packages here: http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/writing-renjin-extensions.html and we have a few example package on GitHub such as rjson <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-json> and xml2 <https://github.com/mjkallen/renjin-xml2> (in various stages of completeness).

Creating these kinds of packages or working on improving Renjin's compatibility with specific CRAN packages are part of our commercial offerings <http://www.renjin.org/support.html> so get in touch with us if you are interested in getting our help.

Maarten

messages.subject: Re: Renjin On Android
messages.body_plain:
Hi Artjom,

I'm afraid I'm not very familiar with Dalvik or Android development, but from googling around it seems that are a few things that Renjin relies on that might be a problem running on Dalvik:

1. Java 7 class file version
2. New Java 7 APIs
3. MethodHandles, new in Java 7
4. Just-in-time JVM Bytecode generation

Issue (1) is what you're encountering with Renjin 0.7.1579, when we actually flipped the switch to compiling all of Renjin to class files with version 1.7, even though we had already started using (2) and (3) previously. This is only a single byte in the .class file, but if it's set then tools limited to supporting Java 1.6 will simply stop.

I'm surprised that (1) and (2) are still issues, again, I don't personally develop on Android, but I have found things like this:
http://tools.android.com/recent/androidstudio032released and https://github.com/yareally/Java7-on-Android

which suggest that the Android tool chain is now capable of handling at least (1) and most of (2). Is it possible for you to use this toolchain or am I missing something?

If you find any new Java 7 API use in Renjin that is a blocker, I'm happy to accept PRs with workarounds or replacements.

MethodHandles (3) are probably a bigger blocker. Up until recently, it was primarily GCC-Bridge which uses MethodHandles to support function pointers in R packages with C and C++ code. If you're don't need such a package, you could work around this by adding an option to GCC-Bridge to generate Java 6 classfiles and fail upon encountering function pointers.

As of very recently <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/0a86ff3379476c24cb3e3c7a901c5e92f57e5376>, however, we've started using GCC-Bridge more centrally in Renjin itself - namely to be able to use the random number generators compiled directly from the GNU R sources, rather than the hand-ported Java versions that we had to maintain ourselves. These function use function pointers/MethodHandles extensively. We could discuss alternate approaches for this but it would take some work. But in the short term, you might consider rebasing your development to 55ef98 <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/55ef9848c25900c618c928c97d030de2243757c9> rather than way back to 0.7.1579.

Finally, Renjin uses (4) JIT bytetcode generation for optimization purposes, currently for combining operations on large vectors, and experimentally, for compiling for loops and other frequently executed code. This in the short term can simply be disabled if Renjin finds itself running under Dalvik, though we are also exploring alternate targets like OpenCL, so why not DEX via something like asmdex.

I think it would be great to see Renjin supported on Android and ideally with a single code base, even if some features might not be supported. Is there any way we could add an integration test to Renjin that could actually test compatibility on each build?

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Updating Renjin's Database packages
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
A while back, Hannes Mulheisen put together Renjin-specific versions of R's database packages, like DBI, RMySQL, MonetDB.R, etc:
https://github.com/hannesmuehleisen/renjin-dbi

Since Renjin didn't support S4 very well at the time, Hannes wrote the new packages using S3, which provided basically the same syntax to the end user. Since then, the OrbisGIS group has done some great work on the drivers for H2 and H2GIS.

However, as we are working to improve compatibility with the BioConductor packages, we've run into several cases where packages expect formal S4 classes like DBIConnection.

Over the next week or two, we'd like to start building the DBI package directly from source as-is, and then release forked versions of RSqlite and RMySQL that just swap out the C bits with a light java wrapper that calls out to JDBC.

This will not only ensure greater interoperability with BioConductor packages, but will help keep these packages in sync with developments to RMySQL and RSqlite etc involve more database-specific functionality like escaping, etc, that our versions don't.

As we make these changes, you can continue to use the versions of RH2 and RH2GIS that are based on Hannes' DBI, but you will need to be careful about transitive dependency conflicts for the next week or two: For example, the following may lead to tears:

library(RH2)  # loads the S3-based RH2 and DBI, so far so good
library(RSQLite) # loads the latest version of RSQLite that expects the new S4-based DBI, fail.

Sorry for the inconvenience, and let us know if you can help with testing these new versions or if you're critically relying on some specific, current behavior.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Migration to GCC-4.7
messages.body_plain:
For anyone who's building from Renjin from source, note that we have just migrated our GCC-Bridge compile from GCC-4.6 to GCC-4.7. If you're building with Vagrant, you can just run

vagrant destroy
vagrant up

For those working on Debian/Ubuntu, you can follow the instructions here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/BUILDING.md#ubuntu-1404

GCC-4.7 is available on the latest LTS release - Ubuntu 16.04 as well as the now aging Ubuntu 14.04 LTS, so this update should keep us chugging along for awhile.

I have however removed the now-outdated instructions for building on OS X. If you're developing on OS X, please bootstrap your build using Vagrant (or submit a PR with instructions on how to get GCC-4.7 and the plugin built!)

If you run into any problems building, don't hesitate to open an issue!

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Updating Renjin's Database packages
messages.body_plain:
Dear Alex,

Thank you for telling us about these information.

RH2GIS is used by our software OrbisGIS. Without RH2GIS we are not able to manage R script between Renjin and our database.
As I wrote in https://github.com/hannesmuehleisen/renjin-dbi/issues/10, we want to improve DBI and support some features like custom table types or geometry type...
Because H2 and H2GIS are java based with have two options :
 - reorganize renjin-dbi to support only the database unsupported by S4-based DB,
 - align H2 and H2GIS with the official R package https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RH2/index.htm

The second option is a bit ugly because of RJDBC, rJava dependencies.

Any comment and proposal are welcome.

Best regards

Erwan

messages.subject: Re: Updating Renjin's Database packages
messages.body_plain:
Hi Erwan,
What we have started to do is move all the core Java glue code from the DBI package to a new library "renjin-jdbc" that can be referenced by the separate database modules:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin-jdbc

I would suggest creating a new repo for the RH2 and RH2GIS modules. The RH2 module contains a good template for defining the S4 classes required for DBI:
https://github.com/dmkaplan2000/RH2/blob/master/R/class.R

Just substitute JDBCDriver for DBIDriver, etc, and replace the rJava calls with calls to JDBCUtils$methodXXX()

Parham is working on the RSQLite module, which might also provide some pointers:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/RSQLite

Best,
Alex

Alex
